lines.say: Something about this girl sleeping on
the dark water feels completely wrong.
This is The Young Martyr,
painted by Paul Delaroche in 1855.
A girl floats on the river
with a halo above her,
while two figures watch from the shore.
But look at her wrists.
Rope ties her hands together.
She doesn't swim. She doesn't struggle.
She simply floats.
According to Roman law under Diocletian,
Christians who would not honour
the gods faced prison or death.
Her faith should have kept her safe.
But she was thrown into the Tiber instead.
And here's the unsettling part.
Her face looks peacefully asleep,
yet her body lies stiff as death.
As if she is both dead and still alive.
So what are those two figures
on the shore really watching?
